description: The MCP tools Uncut gives the agent (Claude Code, Codex, ACP agents). Modules add their own agentTools (e.g. argent_record) on top. Every edit goes through timeline_edit, so it is checked, undoable per turn and attributed.

tools.name: project_read
tools.description: Read the project. 'summary' gives tracks, items with start and length, scenes, media and the revision; 'full' gives project.json. Long videos: pass a range.
tools.returns: revision, duration, and the project summary or full JSON

tools.name: timeline_edit
tools.description: Apply edit ops atomically. Pass the revision you last read; if the user changed the same items since then, the edit is refused and you get the user's changes. One call is one undo step inside your turn. Besides the edit ops, {"op":"insert_device_frame", ...} (see $defs/insertDeviceFrame) puts a device frame with footage under it: the clip on a video track with its box on the frame's screen, the frame on the track above; {"op":"insert_text", "look": ...} (see $defs/insertText) adds text in a look (a text-style module) on a free text track. {"op":"edit_captions", "item": ...} (see $defs/editCaptions) fixes caption words, card starts and settings. {"op":"detach_audio", "item": ...} (see $defs/detachAudio) moves a clip's sound to its own audio item and mutes the clip; {"op":"set_speed", "item": ..., "speed": 2} (see $defs/setSpeed) changes a clip's or audio item's speed, and its length with it. The mix (D83–D88): update_track's mixer {gainDb, pan -1..1, mute, solo, effects} (replaced whole) and update_project's master {gainDb, loudness {targetLufs}, effects} are heard in the preview and mixed the same way in the export. mixer.effects is the track's chain in order: audio.eq (lowCutHz, highCutHz, low/mid/high gainDb and Hz, midQ), audio.compressor (thresholdDb, ratio, attackMs, releaseMs, makeupDb), audio.voice-enhance (amount: high-pass + presence + gentle compression), audio.denoise (amount; applied on export only), audio.duck (under [key track ids], amountDb, attackMs, releaseMs, thresholdDb: the track goes down while a key track has speech, from its measured loudness); each entry may be {"bypass":true}. master.effects holds audio.limiter {ceilingDb} only to change or bypass the limiter (on by default at -1 dBTP); master.loudness.targetLufs is the export dialog's default target (-14 Normal, -16 Quieter, -23 Broadcast, or another number). Looks and effects on a clip (D136) are its effects list, set with update_item: effect.look {look, intensity 0-1}, effect.color (Adjust: exposure in stops, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, vibrance, -1 to 1) and effect.blur, effect.sharpen, effect.vignette, effect.grain, effect.glow, effect.rgb-split, effect.pixelate, effect.mirror, effect.posterize, effect.invert, effect.shake, effect.zoom-pulse, effect.letterbox; modules_list kind "effect" gives each one's params.

summary.description: One line the user sees in the turn card, e.g. 'Cut the shaky parts of the ridge shot'.

tools.returns: the new revision, or a conflict with the user's newer edits, or validation errors

tools.name: render_frames
tools.description: Render frames of the current edit exactly as export would, and return them as images to look at.

phone.description: Draw them 360 px wide, the size of a phone in a feed, to judge readability (overrides scale).

tools.returns: one image per frame

tools.name: contact_sheet
tools.description: One image with a grid of frames, each captioned with its frame and time: from a media file (pulled from the original) or from the edit (drawn as the export draws it). Much cheaper than many render_frames when scanning footage for the good parts. 'every' samples every N frames; without it, 'max' frames (default 24) are spread evenly. 'at: shots' (with media) shows one frame per shot (the middle of each), from the video analysis (run now if needed, cached after). At most 60 cells.

media.description: A media id from project_read. Frames and range are then in project frames of that media (like an item's in).

range.description: Frames [start, end): of the edit, or of the media when media is given. Default: all of it.

every.description: Frames between samples when at is 'every'.

max.description: Most cells (default 24 when every isn't given).

tools.returns: one JPEG (at most 1600 px wide) and, as text, the frame and time of every cell in order (with at: shots, each shot's frames too); at: shots while the analysis still runs: { video: { state: running | queued }, note } (call again)

tools.name: media_analyze
tools.description: Analyse a media file. 'loudness' (also 'silence'): integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness range, true peak and the silences (below -40 dB for at least 0.3 s). 'video' (also 'shots', 'motion', 'stability'): cuts, frozen stretches and, per second, stability (no camera shake), sharpness, exposure and a cleanScore 0-1, with the best stretch inside one shot. Frames in the answer are usable as in. Runs on demand and waits up to about a minute; if the answer says running, call again with the same arguments (it joins the job). Results are cached in .cache/ by the file's content, so asking twice is free. 'transcript': the speech transcribed on this Mac (a summary: language, word, filler and pause counts; transcript_read gives the words). 'beats' (also 'rhythm', 'onsets', 'tempo'): tempo (bpm), a confidence 0-1 and the beats in project frames of the media (the first ones, or those in range with the onsets there). Description comes later.

analyzers.description: Which analyses (default: loudness with silences; name video or beats to get them; video takes longer). silence = loudness; shots, motion, stability = video; rhythm, onsets, tempo = beats.

range.description: Only list silences, cuts, frozen stretches, per-second scores, beats and onsets overlapping these project frames of the media [start, end). The measurement is always of the whole file.

tools.returns: per analyzer (loudness, video, transcript, beats): { state: done | running | queued | failed | cancelled, ... }; loudness when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, integratedLufs, loudnessRangeLu, truePeakDbtp, silence: { thresholdDb, minSeconds, count, ranges: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }] } }; video when done: { cached, hasVideo, seconds, sourceFps, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, ... }, shots, cuts: { threshold, count, list: [{ frame, seconds, score }] }, frozen: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }], drops: [{ frame, seconds, missingSeconds }], stretches: [{ start, end, quality: good | fair | poor, cleanScore }], perSecond: { firstSecond, cleanScore: [], stability: [], sharpness: [], exposure: [], panPerSecond: [] } } (frames are project frames of the media); transcript when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, language, model, words, segments, fillers: { hesitation, maybe }, pauses, pauseSeconds, opening }; beats when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, bpm (null: no steady beat), confidence, beatCount, beatFrames, firstBeat: { frame, seconds }, lastBeat, beats: { frames: [], seconds: [], range?, count?, truncated? }, onsetCount, onsets?: { count, list: [{ frame, seconds, strength }] } (with range) }

tools.name: media_rank
tools.description: Rank video takes by how clean they are: cleanScore 0-1 from stability (no camera shake beyond smooth pans), sharpness (in focus) and exposure, with frozen stretches counted against it. Each take comes with its components (to explain the choice) and its best stretch: the cleanest window seconds inside one shot, as project frames usable as in. Runs or joins the video analysis (cached by content, so asking again is free) and waits up to about a minute; takes still being analysed come back under pending: call again with the same arguments.

media.description: Media ids from project_read. Default: the media imported from folder, or all the project's video.

folder.description: An absolute folder path: rank the project's media whose files are in it (import them first with media_import). Not together with media.

by.description: What to rank by: clean (default, the whole take's cleanScore), best (its best stretch's cleanScore), or one component.

window.description: Length of the best stretch in seconds (default 5).

tools.returns: { by, ranked: [{ rank, media, name, cached, seconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, shots, drops, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen } }], pending?: [{ media, state, progress }], failed?, skipped?, note }

tools.name: transcript_read
tools.description: What's said in a media file, transcribed on this Mac with whisper.cpp (language detected; pass language to force one): text lines with word indices and frames, or each word with its frames; fillers and pauses (at least 0.3 s, aligned to the silences when the loudness analysis is cached) are marked and listed. Paged: pass from = next.from for more. The first call for a file runs the transcription (and the very first one downloads the speech model) and waits up to about a minute; if it answers running, call again with the same arguments. Cached afterwards by the file's content.

range.description: Only words overlapping these project frames of the media [start, end).

format.description: text (default): one line per sentence, 'w<first word index> [start–end] words', {fillers} and (pause n s) inline. words: each word with start and end frames.

from.description: The first word index to list (next.from of the previous page).

language.description: The spoken language as a code (en, pl, ...), or auto (default: detect). A cached transcript in another language is redone.

tools.returns: { media, state, cached, language, model, seconds, words (total), segments, shown: { from, to }, text (format text) | list: [{ i, text, start, end, unsure?, filler? }] (format words), fillers: [{ i, n, text, start, end, kind: hesitation | maybe }], pauses: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, after, edge?, silent? }], next?: { from } } or { transcript: { state: running | queued, progress, stage? } } (frames are project frames of the media)

tools.name: transcript_edit
tools.description: Cut by text: remove words (ranges of transcript_read's word ids), pauses (at least min seconds) and/or hesitation fillers (um, uh, yyy, eee; never the 'maybe' ones) of a media file from every main-track clip that uses it, as one edit on your turn (Undo turn reverts it). Respects each clip's in, length and speed; the main track closes up, items on other tracks don't move. Cuts snap to frames and keep a couple of frames next to the words that stay; adjacent cuts merge; words no longer in the edit are skipped with a note. dryRun returns the plan without changing anything. Gets the transcript like transcript_read (it may have to be made first: if it answers running, call again).

media.description: A media id from project_read; may be left out when exactly one media with sound is on the main track.

remove.description: Word ranges to cut, both ends included, e.g. [{"from": "w12", "to": "w20"}, {"from": "w31"}].

min.description: Pauses at least this many seconds long (default 0.5). A little quiet stays next to each word.

fillers.description: true: also cut the hesitation fillers (English and Polish).

dryRun.description: true: only say what would be cut and the new length.

tools.returns: { media, applied, removed: [{ words?, text, pauses?, fillers?, mediaFrames: { start, end }, frames, seconds, clips }], framesRemoved, secondsSaved, revision, duration, seconds, durationBefore, notes? } (frames: the edit's, mediaFrames: project frames of the media)

tools.name: captions_make
tools.description: Captions from a media file's transcript (D82): a captions item on its own text track that follows the main-track clips using the media, so later cuts, trims, splits and transcript_edit removals keep it in sync and removed words disappear. Words are grouped into cards (1-2 lines, a new card after a pause, a sentence end or the length limits). mode line shows a card at a time, word also accents the speaking word (karaoke), single shows one word at a time. If the media already has captions they're remade from the transcript (corrections kept when the words are the same). Gets the transcript like transcript_read (if it answers running, call again). Fix words, force card starts or change settings afterwards with timeline_edit's edit_captions op; restyle with update_item style (as on text).

media.description: A media id from project_read; may be left out when exactly one media with sound is on the main track.

mode.description: line (default): a card at a time; word: the card with the speaking word accented; single: one word at a time.

look.description: A text-style module id (default text.caption: white lines on dark boxes near the bottom). modules_list kind text-style lists them.

lines.description: How words are grouped (defaults: maxChars what fits the canvas at the look's size, at most 32; maxLines 2, maxSeconds 3, pause 0.3).

hideFillers.description: Leave hesitations (um, uh, yyy) out of the captions.

tools.returns: { media, item, remade, mode, words, cards: [{ from, to, words: 'w12–w18', text }] (the first 40; frames of the edit), cardCount, revision, notes? }

tools.name: subtitles_export
tools.description: Subtitles as a file (D105): the cards every captions item draws (corrections applied, hidden words and fillers left out, word and single modes as whole cards) and the text items of "Subtitles" tracks (an imported .srt / .vtt), merged by time, at the edit's times after cuts. Writes SubRip (.srt) or WebVTT (.vtt); no video is rendered. Refused when there are no captions or subtitles, or when the file exists (pass overwrite).

format.description: srt (default) or vtt; taken from path's extension when it has one.

path.description: An absolute path inside the project folder, ending in .srt or .vtt (default: next to project.json, named after the project). Paths outside it are refused: the user saves elsewhere from the Export dialog.

overwrite.description: Replace a file already there (never a subtitles file the project imported).

tools.returns: { path, format, cues, first: [{ from, to, time, text }] (the first 5; frames of the edit), note }

tools.name: media_import
tools.description: Add footage, music or images from disk to the project's media. Pass path or paths: a file, a folder (the media files directly inside it, not subfolders), or a list of paths. Files are referenced where they are, never copied or changed. At most 50 files per call. Waits for the import and returns each new media entry with its length, size, fps and whether it has sound, plus what was skipped or failed and why. Undo turn removes what it imported.

path.description: An absolute path (or ~/...) to a file or a folder.

name.description: A display name, for a single file only.

tools.returns: revision, imported: [{ id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, fps, width, height, hasAudio }], skipped: [{ path, reason }], failed: [{ path, message }]

tools.name: generate_media
tools.description: Make an image, video or sound with a generator (D99) into Media › Generated, with its prompt, as an edit of this turn. generate.svg is free: pass the SVG or HTML you wrote as content (kind image: a still; kind video: an animation up to 12 s). generate.gpt-image, generate.veo and generate.sound bill the user's own API key; without it the result says which key is needed. Over $1 waits for the user to allow it on a card in the Agent tab.

prompt.description: What to make, in words (stored with the media). For generate.svg, what the content shows.

kind.description: Default: the generator's own (gpt-image image, veo video, sound audio, svg image).

size.description: gpt-image: 1536x1024, 1024x1024 or 1024x1536. veo: 16:9 or 9:16. svg: canvas (default) or WIDTHxHEIGHT.

seconds.description: veo: 4, 6 or 8. sound: 0.5 to 30 (default 5). svg video: up to 12 (default 5).

name.description: The file's name (without extension); default from the prompt.

content.description: generate.svg only: the SVG document or HTML page you wrote (no network, images as data: URLs, system fonts).

tools.returns: id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, width, height, hasAudio, revision, model, estimatedCost (US dollars), turnSpend; or needsKey / approved: false with what to tell the user

tools.name: modules_list
tools.description: Installed modules (transitions, text styles, components, audio effects…) with their params schema, so you know what you can use and how. Components also give their placement (component: default size, devices' screens, animated); showsInPreview says whether the preview draws (or plays) a module as the export does; exportOnly marks an audio effect heard only in the export (noise removal).
tools.returns: manifests

tools.name: graphic_write
tools.description: Write a graphic item's HTML into the project's graphics/ folder, for what the components can't do (D78). The HTML defines render(t, info), called every frame with t = seconds from the item's start and info {frame, fps, duration, width, height, props}; it draws into a transparent canvas-size page. No network, no other files, system fonts only; render must finish within 5 s a frame; the export draws at most 360 distinct frames of one graphic (longer ones hold frames). Files are never overwritten: to change a graphic, write a new name and point the item at it. Then insert {"type":"graphic","src":"graphics/<name>"} on a video track with timeline_edit.

name.description: The file name, e.g. counter.html (it becomes graphics/counter.html).

html.description: The document's body: markup, <style> and a <script> defining render(t, info).

tools.returns: the src to put on the item, or why it was refused

tools.name: ui_show
tools.description: Point the user at something in the editor: move the playhead to a frame, select an item (the timeline and Inspector follow) and/or open a panel. Use it to show a result, e.g. the playhead on the cut you made with that clip selected. Later also to walk the user through doing an edit (D5).

select.description: The id of one timeline item (the editor selects one item at a time).

panel.description: Left: media, text, elements (backgrounds and components), audio. Right: inspector, agent (this chat), checks (the taste checks list).

tools.returns: what was shown

tools.name: project_check
tools.description: Taste checks on the current project (D90), the same list core projectChecks finds: text read time (words ÷ 3 s, 2 s minimum, after the in move), the last text holding 3 s, no new text in the last 2 s, trailing periods, dots or stars between words, filler phrases, frame 1 empty or fading in from black, more than two texts at once, more than one typeface, text under 28 px (at a 1080 px shorter side), text at the frame's edge, mixed footage speeds, the same entrance on every text, long transitions, blank stretches, no sound, music that starts or stops cold, music not ducked under speech, a canvas other than 4:5 (info). Each finding has the rule id, severity (warn or info), one sentence, the item ids, the frame (and range) to look at, and either fix (ops you can send as they are with timeline_edit, with a summary) or a hint. Checks never block the export; rules the project turned off (checks.disabled) are left out.

severity.description: Only warnings, or only info notes.

tools.returns: { revision, warnings, notes, checks: [{ rule, severity, message, items, frame, seconds, range, fix | hint }], disabled }

tools.name: music_list
tools.description: The bundled music library (D91): cozy CC0 tracks (lo-fi, Rhodes, piano), each with id, title, moods, bpm and tempo (slow, medium, fast, free), length in seconds and project frames, loudness (normalised to about -16 LUFS), author and licence, and the media id when it's already in the project. Filter by mood, tempo or words.

mood.description: A mood tag, e.g. warm, calm, lo-fi, upbeat.

tempo.description: slow < 80 bpm, medium 80–109, fast from 110, free = no steady beat.

query.description: Words to find in the title, author or moods.

tools.returns: { tracks: [...] }

tools.name: music_add
tools.description: Add a library track (music_list's id) to the project's media: the file is copied into the project's media/ folder (so the project stays portable) and added as audio media, as an edit on your turn. It returns the media id and its length in project frames; then put it on an audio track with timeline_edit (an audio item with fades, often ducked under the voice). A track already in the project returns its media id without copying again.

id.description: The library track id, e.g. cozy-2.

tools.returns: { media, frames, seconds, revision }

tools.name: library_search
tools.description: Search the sound library (D134): royalty-free music or sound effects online (Openverse without a key, or Freesound when the user stored a Freesound key), CC0 and CC BY only (both allow commercial use; CC BY needs credit, project_read lists it), or with source "included" Uncut's bundled CC0 sound effects. Search by what it sounds like: whoosh, ui click, impact, riser, notification, applause, bass boom, bruh, airhorn, record scratch, sad trombone; for music a genre or mood (lofi, ambient, cinematic, upbeat piano) and songs true for full songs. Openverse allows 20 searches a minute and 200 a day for everyone on this connection, cached for 30 minutes: search with purpose, don't page through results needlessly.

query.description: What to search for. Required unless source is included.

license.description: cc0: only sounds that need no credit.

length.description: short < 30 s, medium 30 s to 2 min, long > 2 min.

category.description: source included: whoosh, transition, ui, impact, riser, notification, crowd or meme.

tools.returns: { hits: [{ id, title, creator, seconds, frames, license, tags }], total, page, pages } or, for included, { sounds }

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Add a library_search result to the project's media: the file is downloaded (or a bundled sound copied) into the project's media/ folder and added as audio media with its credits (source, creator, licence, attribution), as an edit on your turn. Returns the media id and length; then put it on an audio track with timeline_edit. A sound already in the project returns its media id.

id.description: A hit id from library_search, e.g. openverse:eab8a6e2-0ac8-4615-9e0d-ebde30523783, freesound:351256 or sfx:bass-boom.

tools.returns: { media, path, frames, seconds, license, revision }

tools.name: screen_record
tools.description: Record the user's screen or a window (a browser window shows as its page title) on this Mac for some seconds, as media of this turn (D144). The user is always asked first on a card in the Agent tab, where they pick the screen or window (yours preselected by name) and can say no; nothing is ever recorded without their Record. The result gives the media id and the source's name, or that the user said no.

source.description: The screen or window to suggest, by (part of) its name, e.g. "Chrome" or "Screen 1". The user can pick another.

seconds.description: How long to record, after a 3-2-1 countdown.

tools.returns: id, name, path, frames, seconds, width, height, source, revision; or approved: false with what to tell the user

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question on a card in the Agent tab and wait for the answer (up to 15 minutes): options to pick (one, or several with multi) and/or their own words. Use it before building whenever something material is unclear or missing (the brand, the logo, the audience, the length, the format, the real assets) instead of guessing or inventing.

freeText.description: A box for their own answer (default true; always on without options).

tools.returns: the picked options and the text, or that it was skipped

tools.name: brief_write
tools.description: Save the production brief (brief.json in the project), shown to the user as a Brief card they can edit. Co-write it with the user before building a new video; write it again when it changes.

assets.description: The real assets it uses (recordings, screenshots, the kit's logo).

tools.returns: saved, or what's missing

tools.name: storyboard_propose
tools.description: Propose the storyboard / shot list for the user to approve on a card before you build (it waits up to 15 minutes). Each beat: start and end in seconds, entry and exit states, purpose, real assets, the sound it lands on. The answer is approved (maybe with beats the user edited: build those), or a change the user asked for (propose again).

start.description: Seconds from the start of the video.

entry.description: What's on screen as the beat starts.

exit.description: What's on screen as it ends (the next beat's entry).

purpose.description: Why the beat is there: what the viewer gets from it.

assets.description: The real assets it shows (media names, kit logo, recordings).

sound.description: The beat, downbeat or hit it lands on.

tools.returns: approved with the beats to build, or the change asked for

tools.name: review_submit
tools.description: Submit a critic review round of the built video (after a contact_sheet of the edit and render_frames with phone true in this turn): scores 0–10 for the hook in the first 2 s, readability at phone size, motion, variety, sound sync and brand accuracy, and the worst defects with their time. Uncut checks graphics for determinism (each drawn twice at the same frame) and saves the round; the answer says whether to fix and review again.
tools.returns: the round, its scores, the determinism check and what to do next

tools.name: brand_read
tools.description: Read the project's brand kit (colours with roles, fonts, logos, tone, taglines, URLs, do's and don'ts, style guide) and skills, or one of the kit's files: a logo or example frame comes back as an image (SVG as text) with its path for media_import. Without an active kit it lists the kits there are.

kit.description: A kit id (default: the project's kit).

file.description: A file of the kit, e.g. its logos.light name.

tools.returns: the kit and skills, or the file

tools.name: brand_write
tools.description: Write into a brand kit: a style guide (from a reference), colours, fonts, tone and the rest, merged into what's there (a field you pass replaces that field). With a new name and no kit, makes a new kit (scope project by default) and makes it the project's kit. Only what the user gave or approved, never invented brand facts.
tools.returns: the kit as saved

tools.name: reference_frames
tools.description: A contact sheet of a reference video or image file on disk that isn't in the project (it isn't imported): frames spread over its length, for reading a style (palette, type, shot lengths, transitions, camera, grain) without copying its content.
tools.returns: the sheet with each cell's time, the file's length and size

tools.name: beat_grid
tools.description: The beat grid of the music on the timeline in timeline frames: tempo, beats, downbeats (bar starts, the strongest beat of each 4) and the strongest hits, from the beats analysis; with snap, each frame you give with the nearest beat and downbeat, to put cuts and state changes on the beat and big moments on a downbeat.

item.description: An audio item (default: the longest music on the timeline).

tools.returns: tempo, beats, downbeats and hits in timeline frames, and the snaps

insertText.description: Text in a look (a text-style module, D80), as one op: the item gets the look's size, weight, position and in/out moves (the rest of the look, e.g. its outline, shadow or box, applies while the item doesn't set those fields), plus the looks it comes with (a kicker above a title) on their own text tracks; it goes on the top-most text track free for [start, start + duration), else a new one on top.

look.description: A text-style module id, e.g. text.big-title, text.caption, text.boxed-label (modules_list kind text-style lists them with their looks).

text.description: Markup: **bold**, [[accent]], `mono`, \n for a line break. Default: the look's placeholder.

id.description: The new item's id (default: the look's name, numbered).

style.description: Style fields over the look's, canvas px: size, weight, font, color, align, tracking, lineHeight, uppercase, stroke {width, color}, shadow {x, y, blur, color, opacity}, background {color, opacity, padding, radius, wrap box|lines}; false for stroke, shadow or background removes the look's.

transform.description: The text box's top-left and width in canvas px, over the look's.

animation.description: In/out moves instead of the look's (frames), or null for none.

alone.description: Leave out the looks it comes with.

detachAudio.description: Detach audio (D123): the clip's sound becomes an audio item (same media, in point, speed and start; the clip's volume, fades and volume keys move to it) on the first audio track free for that stretch (or a new one, or `track`), and the clip gets mute: true. Captions and transcript cuts keep following the clip on main.

id.description: The new audio item's id (default audio-N).

track.description: An audio track that is free there (default: picked or made).

setSpeed.description: Change the speed of a clip or an audio item (D125): 0.1 to 10 (2 = twice as fast). It keeps playing the same stretch of its media, so its duration becomes duration x old speed / new speed (main clips after it ripple; on a free track the next item must leave room). keepPitch false lets the pitch follow the speed (like tape); true keeps it (the default).

editCaptions.description: Change a captions item (D82) as one op: fix words (by transcript_read's word id; "" hides a word, null goes back to the transcript's), force a new card at a word (or stop forcing one), switch the mode, change the grouping or hide fillers. It becomes one update_item.

on.description: true (default): a card starts at this word; false: no forced start.

lines.description: Grouping settings over the item's (null for a field: its default): maxChars, maxLines (1 or 2), maxSeconds, maxWords, pause.

cover.description: true: stretch the captions over the whole main track again (after clips were added past them).

insertDeviceFrame.description: A device frame (component.device-frame) with footage under it, as one op: the footage is a clip on a free video track above main (else a new one), its box the frame's screen (cover, the screen's rounded corners); the frame goes on the video track above it; both from start for duration. Default box: centred, 86% of the canvas height (a browser 80% of its width).

media.description: Video or image media for the screen; leave it out for the frame alone.

in.description: Where the clip starts in its media (project frames).

box.description: The frame's box in canvas pixels: x, y (its top-left) and h (the width follows the device's shape).

color.description: The frame's colour (a theme token or CSS colour).

url.description: browser: the address in its bar.

hold.description: Footage shorter than the frame holds its last frame (a freeze) instead of looping.
